history.p: When the popular King Frederik V passed away in January 1766, Scheibe was asked to provide music for the funeral service. In order to find a poet who could write the text, a competition was set up. The young Johannes Ewald was chosen and the two started their fruitful collaboration. Apparently the work made a great impression, especially the Arioso for soprano ‘Hold, Taare op at trille’ (Stop tear to trickle). For the event also Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock wrote an elegy (Rothschilds Gräber, 1766). Later Scheibe used some of the movements in the Passion cantata ‘Vor Harpe er bleven til Sorrig’ (SchW B2:306), and this popular movement was also included (no. 19). As Scheibe was not the official head of The Royal Orchestra, he sent a list of expenses to the Lord Chamberlain, Adam Gottlob Moltke, who was so shocked that he set up a commission in order to determine the appropriate fees. The auditors’ argument was that the funeral service for King Christian VI in 1746, for which Scheibe also composed the music, had been much cheaper. According to Scheibe’s detailed reports he held more than thirty hours of rehearsals, employed fifty musicians and twenty-four singers of which none were ‘dilettantes’, and defended the musicians’ wages which he thought were fair taking into account the inflation. The auditors argued that since Scheibe already received a pension he was not entitled to a fee. The disagreement, which might also have been due to Moltke’s declining influence at court and hence an attempt to retain power, seems to have been settled in the early autumn. The only surviving musical source is the present professional transcript most likely produced in the late 1770s, perhaps even after Scheibe’s death.

annot.p: 'I Morgen Onsdag Eftermiddag Klokken 1, bliver i Frue-Kirke giort Prøve paa den af Hr. Capellmester Scheibe componerede prægtige Vocal- og Instrumental Sørge-Musiqve, som skal opføres i Christiansborgs Slots-Kirke paa den Dag, da den Høysalige Konges Liig bliver udført.'
'I Formiddags blev i Frue Kirke atter giort Prøve paa Hr. Capellmester Scheibes forhen ommeldte Sørge-Musiqve og paa Onsdag Eftermiddag Klokken 1 [?]. bliver atter Prøve foretaget sammesteds.'

'Alle Stadens Klokker begynder i Morgen om Eftermiddagen (som i forrige No. er meldt) at ringe Klokken 1. og vedvarer til Klokken 3. Derpaa begynder Klage-Tienesten i Slots-Capellet med Sang og Musiqve. - Hr. Johannes Ewald, en Søn af Hr. Professor Ewald, har forfattet Sørge-Sangen, og den Kongl. Capellmester Hr. Johan Adolph Scheibe Musiqven.'

'Die Poesie zu dieser Cantate rühret vom Herrn J. Ewald her. Sie ist wirklich schön. Wir wollen unsern Lesern nicht eben die beste, sondern nur die erste Stelle, die uns in die Hände fällt, zur Probe mittheilen: ein Recitativ, das von dem Frieden gesungen wird [...]'.

physDesc.watermark: at least two distinct types are found: 1) paste-down: countermark is 'J Honig & Zoonen' though the beehive emblem corresponds to Heawood:54; 2) music: consists of the countermark 'J H & Z' (J. Honig and Zoon/Zoonen) corresponding to Heawood:1562, may be dated to around 1787 or even later (cf. Churchill:15). Hence it is possible that the source is a later copy of the original.
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o; upright format; front paste-down, neither front nor end flyleaves; title page (fol. 1r), list of instruments and choirs (fol. 1v), music (fols. 2r–96v; pp. [2]–192) with pages numbered in contemporary pencil, fol. 97r with empty staves but unnumbered, end paste-down; in all 97 folios. Hand-ruled paper, 14, 16, 20 staves (8 mm; single rastrum used) in brown ink and music in black ink. A fairly clean copy with only few additions in pencil such as page numbering and a few bar numbers; includes some corrections or changes to the music in ink. Dynamics and slurring seems to have been added at a later date in a lighter, brown ink; some of the original markings in black ink have been cancelled and changes added.
Original half-binding with leather spine and corners with dark greyish marbled board with label on front cover: 'H. & Fr. Rungs Musik-Arkiv. | Partitur. No. 255'.
